title: CI: add ephemeral integration plan/apply harness w/ region + NAT matrix, provider caching, and retries
author: Sahana Iyer
description:
This adds an integration test harness for the Terraform module set that performs an ephemeral plan+apply in a sandbox AWS account and then destroys the resources. The goal is to catch provider/order-of-operations issues (esp. endpoints) and ensure our module composition works across a small supported topology matrix.

What this PR adds: (1) GitHub Actions workflow `terraform-integration.yml` that runs `terraform fmt`/`validate`/`tflint`/`checkov` and then an ephemeral apply+destroy test in an isolated sandbox account via GitHub OIDC AssumeRole. (2) A matrix that exercises: regions [us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1] x NAT mode [single, per_az] (and a minimal `nat_mode=none` run for the locked-down example behind a feature flag). (3) Provider/plugin caching via `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` and `actions/cache` keyed by `hashFiles('**/.terraform.lock.hcl')` to keep runtime/cost manageable. (4) Retry/wait logic around known AWS eventual consistency hotspots (interface endpoint association, route table propagation) and a hard guarantee that destroy runs even if apply fails.

Notes/constraints: - The integration apply only runs for PRs from the main repo (not forks) and uses the `redwood-terraform-sandbox` environment with required reviewers. - Resources are tagged with `redwood:ci=true`, `redwood:pr=<num>`, `redwood:owner=ci` for cost tracking/cleanup. - Workflow includes a budget/time guard: per-matrix job timeout 35m and a max-parallel of 2 to avoid bursting NAT/EIP usage.

Follow-ups: This harness surfaced a flake in endpoint creation ordering (see SUP-2204); we added retries here and will still fix the underlying dependency ordering in the module code in a separate PR.

Test plan: - Verified locally with `./ci/integration/run.sh` against a dev sandbox role (single region) - Ran CI twice; first run caught an intermittent endpoint association failure; second run passed after adding retries - Verified destroy executes on apply failures by forcing an invalid var and confirming cleanup step ran.

Release notes: Adds ephemeral integration apply coverage to CI (no user-facing module behavior changes).

conversation: Victor Alvarez (review): Matrix looks good. Two asks: (1) please cap parallelism; per-AZ NAT in 3 regions can burn EIPs quickly if we parallelize too hard. (2) ensure we always destroy even on apply failure; I’ve seen other repos leak NAT gateways on errors.
Sahana Iyer (author): Good call. Added `strategy.max-parallel: 2` and moved destroy into `if: always()` with a separate step that runs even if apply fails. Also tagging resources for easy cleanup.

Kevin Osei (review): For OIDC role permissions: please document the minimal IAM actions required + confirm CloudTrail/audit expectations. We should avoid giving broad `*` for EC2/VPC. Also, can we ensure the workflow only runs from this repo and requires environment approval?

Sahana Iyer (author): Updated `ci/integration/README.md` with a minimal policy outline and explicitly calls out that the sandbox account owns the role/policy (no customer guidance). Workflow now gates apply behind `environment: redwood-terraform-sandbox` with required reviewers and includes a fork check so PRs from forks won’t execute apply.

Irene Choi (review): Caching: the cache key should include lockfile(s) only, otherwise it’ll thrash. Also `terraform init` needs `-upgrade=false` to avoid changing provider versions in CI unexpectedly.

Sahana Iyer (author): Done. Cache key now hashes `**/.terraform.lock.hcl` and the runner pins `terraform init -upgrade=false`. We also export `TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1` and `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` consistently.

Bruno Silva (review): Integration script: the retry loop should only wrap `apply` and not `init`/`plan`. Also add a short sleep between retries and print a concise summary of the last error to make logs readable.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated: only `apply` is retried (max 3), exponential backoff with jitter, and we tail the last ~200 lines on failure. Added a note about AWS endpoint eventual consistency.
GitHub Actions (bot): integration apply/destroy (us-west-2, nat=per_az) failed: Timeout waiting for VPC endpoint association (InvalidVpcEndpointId.NotFound).

Sahana Iyer (author): Added stabilization wait: after endpoint creation, we poll `describe-vpc-endpoints` until state=available before proceeding, and added a small delay before route association steps. Re-ran failing job; now green.
Victor Alvarez (approval): Approved. Thanks for the guardrails and `always()` destroy; this will save us a lot of pain.
Kevin Osei (approval): Approved with the environment gating + fork protections in place.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Sahana Iyer into main
